title: dutiyasandiṭṭhikasutta
credit: English: course exercise book, after Bhikkhu Bodhi, The Numerical Discourses of the Buddha (Wisdom Publications, 2012).

paras.en:
Then a certain brahmin approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he exchanged greetings with the Blessed One … and he sat down to one side. Seated to one side, that brahmin said this to the Blessed One:
“It is said: ‘The directly visible Dhamma, the directly visible Dhamma,’ Master Gotama. In what way, Master Gotama, is the Dhamma directly visible, timeless, a ‘come and see’ matter, applicable, to be personally understood by the wise?”

“Well then, brahmin, I will question you about this. As you see fit, so you should answer. What do you think, brahmin? (1) When there is lust within you, do you know: ‘There is lust within me,’ and when there is no lust within you, do you know: ‘There is no lust within me’?”
“Yes, sir.”

“Since, brahmin, when there is lust within you, you know: ‘There is lust within me,’ and when there is no lust within you, you know: ‘There is no lust within me,’ in this way the Dhamma is directly visible …

“What do you think, brahmin? (2) When there is hatred within you … (3) … when there is delusion within you … (4) … when there is a bodily fault within you … (5) … when there is a verbal fault within you … (6) … when there is a mental fault within you, do you know: ‘There is a mental fault within me,’ and when there is no mental fault within you, do you know: ‘There is no mental fault within me’?”
“Yes, sir.”

“Since, brahmin, when there is a mental fault within you, you know: ‘There is a mental fault within me,’ and when there is no mental fault within you, you know: ‘There is no mental fault within me,’ in this way the Dhamma is directly visible, timeless, a ‘come and see’ matter, applicable, to be personally understood by the wise.”
“Excellent, Master Gotama! Excellent, Master Gotama! … Let Master Gotama consider me a lay follower who from today has gone for refuge as long as I have life.”
